I have been farming these 20 mu for 15 years now, and I know this land well. My family has six mouths to feed, and with some of them working off-farm, I cannot waste labor on things that do not pay. I have a well, so water is there when I need it, but pumping costs money and time, so I only irrigate when the crops truly need it.

It is autumn now, time to plant winter wheat. I will put wheat on all 20 mu because the wheat-maize rotation is what this soil is made for. Before sowing, I will hire the rotary tiller to go over the fields — 50 yuan per mu, but it gives a good seedbed and everyone in the village does it. For seed, I will buy an improved variety from the supply shop, maybe Jimai 22 or Shixin, whatever the dealer says is reliable this year. I do not trust saved seed anymore; the bagged seed sprouts better and resists disease. I will spread about 50 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as basal dressing at sowing, and then in the spring when the wheat starts jointing, I will topdress with urea. For the whole season, that works out to roughly 15 jin of pure nitrogen, 6 jin of phosphorus, and 4 jin of potassium per mu. I will irrigate three times: once before winter if the autumn is dry, once at jointing in March, and once during grain filling in May. For spraying, I will do a pre-emergence or early spring herbicide, one or two insecticide sprays if aphids come, and a fungicide if leaf rust shows up — about three trips total. If the weather cooperates, I expect around 500 kg per mu.

After harvesting the wheat in early June, I will plant summer maize immediately — no time to waste. I will use a no-till planter right behind the combine. Everyone here switched to no-tillage for maize years ago; it saves diesel, keeps moisture in the ground, and lets me plant fast. I will buy hybrid seed, probably Denghai 605 or something similar, one bag does about one mu. At planting I will put down compound fertilizer, then at the big-flare stage I will side-dress more urea. That comes to about 14 jin nitrogen, 5 jin phosphorus, and 4 jin potassium per mu. I will irrigate twice: once when the plants are knee-high if June is dry, and once at grain filling in August. I will spray herbicide right after emergence, and insecticide two or three times for corn borer and armyworm — three applications in total. A normal year should give me about 550 kg per mu.
